memories.content: The user stores copies of identity documents in an encrypted folder.
On a day the user transferred between buses twice, they rested for an hour after the trip.
On a day the user took a direct route with a similar travel time, they remained seated to the destination.
After arriving at an entrance with stairs only, the user went around to an entrance on the other side of the building.
On a day the user checked the accessible entrance location in advance, they arrived before the agreed time.
On a rainy day, the user's clothes became wet while crossing an uncovered section at a transfer stop.
On a day the user traveled with their maternal uncle, they agreed to meet at an entrance near the elevator.
The user's maternal uncle prefers an aisle seat from which it is easy to stand during long-distance travel.
The local agent cannot know whether an accessible entrance is operating that day from past route records alone.
The transfer route the user takes has more boarding and alighting events and walking segments than the direct route.
The user stores prepared meals on the second shelf of the freezer.
The user went to the market without a shopping list and bought onions that were already at home.
On a day the user shopped after checking a refrigerator photo, they did not make a duplicate purchase.
On a day the user made a spicy stew, they left part of one bowl uneaten.
The next time the user cooked it, they used half as much chili powder and finished the meal.
When cooking with their younger brother, the user assigned the cooking sequence only verbally and they did the same task twice.
The next time, the user and their younger brother split ingredient preparation and heat control and finished the meal 20 minutes earlier.
When cooking together, the user's younger brother prefers to divide the cooking and dishwashing roles in advance.
The local agent can compare responses across several meals, but it cannot conclude from one unfinished food item that the user dislikes that ingredient.
The condition of frozen prepared food may vary with its packaging and storage duration.

analysis.overview: The frames cover separate domains: the reference frame concerns travel accessibility, route burden, and document storage, while the compared frame concerns food storage, shopping, meal adjustment, and shared cooking. Their inference cautions are analogous in form but govern different decisions, so no cross-frame semantic relation is established.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful document-security practice with no corresponding claim in the compared frame.
relations.summary: The user keeps copies of identity documents in encrypted storage.

relations.reason: These memories split one reference-only comparison of travel-route demands; the compared frame contains no travel-route claim.
relations.summary: The transfer and direct-route observations jointly characterize differing boarding, walking, seating, and post-trip experiences.

relations.reason: This is a separate reference-only observation about weather exposure during travel.
relations.summary: An uncovered section at a transfer stop exposed the user to rain.

relations.reason: These memories provide complementary episodes about finding or checking an accessible entrance, with no counterpart in the compared frame.
relations.summary: The user's experiences connect accessible-entrance location knowledge with building approach and arrival outcomes.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful reference-only travel arrangement.
relations.summary: The user and their maternal uncle arranged to meet near an elevator entrance while traveling together.

relations.reason: This is a separate reference-only seating preference.
relations.summary: The user's maternal uncle prefers an aisle seat that permits easy standing on long journeys.

relations.reason: This reference-only epistemic limit governs accessibility-status inference, whereas the compared frame's inference limit concerns food preference and therefore addresses a different operational decision.
relations.summary: Past route records alone cannot establish whether an accessible entrance is operating on a particular day.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful compared-only food-storage location.
relations.summary: The user stores prepared meals on the freezer's second shelf.

relations.reason: These memories split one compared-only claim about pre-shopping inventory awareness.
relations.summary: The shopping episodes indicate that checking existing supplies can distinguish duplicate purchasing from avoiding it.

relations.reason: These memories form one compared-only observation about adjusting a recipe after an unfinished meal.
relations.summary: The meal episodes associate reducing chili powder with finishing a stew that had previously been left partly uneaten.

relations.reason: These memories collectively describe one compared-only coordination pattern involving the user's younger brother.
relations.summary: The shared-cooking observations concern advance role division as a way to avoid duplicated work and improve completion time.

relations.reason: This compared-only epistemic limit governs inference about food preference, not the accessibility-status decision covered by the reference frame.
relations.summary: One unfinished food item is insufficient evidence that the user dislikes an ingredient, although responses across meals can be compared.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful compared-only qualification about frozen-food condition.
relations.summary: Packaging and storage duration can affect the condition of frozen prepared food.

reports.compared_only: Compared-only information covers freezer organization, duplicate-purchase prevention, adjusting spice levels, coordinating shared cooking, cautious interpretation of unfinished food, and variables affecting frozen meals.
reports.reference_only: Reference-only information covers protected document storage, route and weather burdens, accessible-entrance planning, travel arrangements and seating preferences, plus limits on predicting entrance operation.
